title: Who's Who: Éloise Varenne
summary: Natural philosopher whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Éloise Varenne (1719–1784) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a natural philosopher whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Varenne gave Eidetics its first useful hypothesis in 1756: enduring things might have deeper Referents, with material objects expressing them imperfectly. Her proposal that shape should matter more than substance could be tested.
She spent her later years defending that distinction from both mystics and impatient experimentalists.

For Alderwick readers, Éloise Varenne is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
